$comment: Registry of BUILT widgets, consumed by the gallery page and scripts/build.mjs. `title` is the gallery card AND the page heading: they used to be allowed to differ, the card naming the topic and the page asking the question, and that split was cut — a student who clicked "Hypothesis Testing" should land on a page that says so. `npm run check` asserts manifest.title === defineWidget({title}) === the index.html <title> prefix; the question belongs in `subtitle`. `blurb` is gallery copy and nothing else reads it. The plan — every candidate concept, its target misconception and evidence — lives in docs/catalogue.md; see that file for why the two are separate. A widget marked shipped there must appear here, and vice versa. This is now the ONLY place a widget height is recorded; it used to be three, and deleting the embedders closed that seam.

widgets.title: The Normal Distribution
widgets.blurb: Many small random nudges, added together, land in a bell curve.

widgets.title: Central Limit Theorem
widgets.blurb: The mean of a sample goes normal whatever the population looks like.

widgets.title: Bootstrap Sampling
widgets.blurb: Resample your one sample to see how uncertain its mean really is.

widgets.title: Confidence Intervals
widgets.blurb: Build the same studies' intervals three ways — bootstrap, normal, t — and watch how often each actually contains the true mean. At n = 5 the normal one misses far more than 1 time in 20.

widgets.title: Hypothesis Testing
widgets.blurb: Shuffle the group labels to see what chance alone could have produced.

widgets.title: Multiple Testing
widgets.blurb: Test twenty thousand genes at p < 0.05 and about a thousand come back significant even when none of them is different. Then see what correcting for it costs.

widgets.title: Power and Error Rates
widgets.blurb: You choose the false positive rate; you do not choose the other one. Change the sample size and watch which of the two moves — and which does not budge.

widgets.title: Maximum Likelihood
widgets.blurb: Twelve gene counts, drawn once. Try a candidate mean and every count gets a height under it; multiply them and you have how probable that candidate makes exactly what you saw. Then estimate the dispersion the Poisson ignored, and watch a search over both stop moving after two steps.
